advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reap git's process group in run_git_reaped on any exception from communicate, not only TimeoutExpired, then re-raise.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:294: start_new_session=(os.name == "posix"),
src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:296-302: `try: stdout, stderr = proc.communicate(timeout=timeout)` / `except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: reap_process_group(...)` — no handler for any other exception
Absence: no `except BaseException` / `finally` reaping in run_git_reaped, unlike stdlib subprocess.run, which kills the child on any exception before re-raising
src/rebar/_store/event_commit_git.py:220: run_auto_maintenance catches only OSError, so the exception propagates while the caller's write lock unwinds
advisory.finding: run_git_reaped reaps the process group only on subprocess.TimeoutExpired. Any other exception during proc.communicate (KeyboardInterrupt, or a SystemExit raised from a signal handler) leaves the git maintenance child running. Because start_new_session=True puts git in its own session, terminal SIGINT no longer reaches it. The parent then unwinds and releases the write lock while the repack keeps going outside the lock. Before this change subprocess.run killed the child on any exception, so the new code is weaker on this path.
scenarios: An operator presses Ctrl-C during a slow incremental-repack. Python raises KeyboardInterrupt, the write lock is released, and git (in its own session, so it never got the SIGINT) keeps repacking while the next writer commits.
A shutdown handler raises SystemExit in the main thread during the maintenance step, which leaves an orphaned repack and possibly a stranded maintenance.lock.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `except BaseException: reap_process_group(proc, grace=_REAP_GRACE_S, drain=_REAP_DRAIN_S, label="git", logger=logger); raise` after the TimeoutExpired handler.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Log a warning from run_auto_maintenance when the result is None, returncode 124 or non-zero, and ideally when objects/maintenance.lock exists before the run.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:99: `run_auto_maintenance(tracker)` — return value ignored
src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:120: `run_auto_maintenance(tracker_dir)` — return value ignored
src/rebar/_store/event_commit_git.py:216-221: returns the result or None, with no logging
src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:302: the timeout path returns _timed_out(...) without logging
The ADR amendment says a stranded maintenance.lock makes `maintenance run --auto` exit 0 doing nothing, and no check here looks for that lock
advisory.finding: The explicit maintenance step is still fail-open: both callers discard run_auto_maintenance's result, and neither run_auto_maintenance nor run_git_reaped logs a timeout (124), a non-zero exit, or a launch failure (None). A step that times out after every write, or always fails, looks exactly like a healthy one. That is the same invisibility that let the step be a silent no-op for two months.
scenarios: incremental-repack grows past 120 s on a bigger store. Every write then holds the lock for about 130 s, with no log line naming the cause.
maintenance.lock gets stranded again by a hard kill during the step. Maintenance silently stops, as in the original incident.
advisory.suggested_fix: In run_auto_maintenance, check the result: when it is None or result.returncode != 0, call logger.warning with the returncode and a stderr excerpt before returning.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Route project_ensures' raw git commit (and similar raw store commits) through the suppressed env, or narrow the doc claim to bounded children.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/project_ensures.py:42-44: `return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", tracker, *args], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)`
src/rebar/_store/project_ensures.py:81-88: `_git(tracker, "commit", "-q", "--no-verify", ...)`
docs/concurrency.md (changed hunk): "The store's only maintenance is the explicit post-write step"
src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:205: comment says "the store's only maintenance is the explicit, write-locked ... step"
advisory.finding: The change says the explicit step is the store's only maintenance, but some store git calls bypass run_git_bounded and so never get the new environment suppression. For example, project_ensures._git runs a raw unbounded `git commit` with no maintenance.auto/gc.auto override, so it can still start a foreground `maintenance run --auto` (a full gc on a large store) during container start-up ensures.
scenarios: A first start on a store with no projects.json runs the seed commit, which can start a full gc on a 1M-object store with no bound and outside the write lock.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the explicit-step test show that commit-graph and incremental-repack ran (e.g. a commit-graph file exists, or the traced maintenance argv includes all three --task flags), and give the 'no gc' check a world in which it can fail
evidence: assert int(stats["in-pack"]) >= 300, stats
assert "gc" not in started, "the explicit step must not run gc's reachability walk"
src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py: run_git_reaped passes `env=_without_implicit_maintenance(None, args)`, which sets gc.auto=0, so even a `--task=gc` under `--auto` would never start gc
No assertion anywhere checks for a commit-graph file or a multi-pack-index/incremental pack, and none inspects the traced maintenance argv for the task flags
advisory.finding: The explicit-step test only shows that the loose-objects task ran. Removing `--task=commit-graph` or `--task=incremental-repack` from `_MAINTENANCE_TASKS` would leave every test green. Its 'no gc' assertion also cannot fail as set up: run_git_reaped injects gc.auto=0, and the fixture's 300 loose objects are below gc's auto threshold anyway.
scenarios: A refactor shrinks _MAINTENANCE_TASKS to ("--task=loose-objects",); packs then pile up outside the multi-pack-index, as in the production incident, and the suite stays green
advisory.suggested_fix: From the trace, take the `maintenance run` argv and assert it contains all of `--task=commit-graph`, `--task=loose-objects` and `--task=incremental-repack`. Alternatively, after the run, assert `objects/info/commit-graph` (or `objects/info/commit-graphs`) exists.

advisory.finding: No test checks the new `-c maintenance.auto=false -c gc.auto=0` on the container start-up fetch in reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh. The existing ensure-script tests never mention maintenance.
scenarios: Someone later drops the `-c` pair from the start-up fetch. The container fetch then starts a foreground full gc outside the write lock again, and no test catches it.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a table case for a malformed/empty inherited GIT_CONFIG_COUNT (e.g. "" -> suppression appended at index 0; "x" -> env passed through)
evidence:
if not count_text.isdigit():
        return merged
Tests cover only GIT_CONFIG_COUNT="1" (test_bounded_git_child_disables_implicit_maintenance_after_inherited_config) and the `config` exemption
advisory.finding: No test covers the branch of `_without_implicit_maintenance` that returns the env unchanged when the inherited GIT_CONFIG_COUNT is not a digit string. With an input such as GIT_CONFIG_COUNT="x", the child gets no suppression at all, and nothing pins that this is deliberate.
scenarios: Inherited GIT_CONFIG_COUNT="x": git rejects the env, but a refactor that silently ignores the malformed count would also go unnoticed

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 204 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug 51e0-5038-bf00-4653 has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix like this is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan 51e0-5038-bf00-4653` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review 51e0-5038-bf00-4653` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan 51e0-5038-bf00-4653 --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.
